title: Module 9: Security & Entitlements 🛡️
content: Welcome to Module 9!
In this session, we will explore how AMPS keeps your data safe and ensures that only the right people have access to the right resources.
Topic coverage:
• Authentication & Logon
• Resource Entitlements
• Content-Based Security
• Field-Level Security
• Enterprise Integration Modules

title: The Security Trinity 🔒
content: AMPS security is built on three pillars:
1. **Authentication**: Who are you? (Identity Verification)
2. **Entitlement**: What are you allowed to do? (Access Control)
3. **Encryption**: Keeping data private in transit (TLS/SSL)
Built with a plugin-based architecture for maximum flexibility! 🔌

title: Authentication Flow 🔑
content: How AMPS verifies your identity when you connect.
mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant AMPS
    participant AuthModule
    participant IDP as Identity Provider

    Client->>AMPS: Connect & Logon(user, pass)
    AMPS->>AuthModule: authenticate(user, pass)
    AuthModule->>IDP: Validate Credentials
    IDP-->>AuthModule: Success/Fail
    AuthModule-->>AMPS: Authenticated User Context
    AMPS-->>Client: Logon Acknowledged

title: Logon Methods: Explicit vs. Implicit 📋
content: **Explicit Logon**: The client sends a `logon` command with credentials immediately after connecting. (Recommended! ✅)
**Implicit Logon**: The client sends a command (like `subscribe`) without logging in first. AMPS tries to authenticate with an empty username/password.
⚠️ Implicit logon is **disabled by default** in modern AMPS for better security.

title: Entitlements Overview 🚦
content: Entitlements are the 'Gatekeepers' of AMPS.
They control access to every operation:
• Can this user subscribe to this topic?
• Can they publish to that queue?
• Are they allowed to see the admin console?
Checked at the start of a command and cached for performance! ⚡

title: Resource Types & Permissions 🎫
content: AMPS categorizes resources into four main types:
• **logon**: Permission to enter the system.
• **topic**: Access to message data (read/write).
• **admin**: Access to statistics and management commands.
• **replication_logon**: Permission for other AMPS instances to connect.
Permissions can be `read`, `write`, or `none`.

title: Entitlement Check Flow 🔄
content: AMPS checks permissions for every resource access.
mermaid:
graph TD
    A[Client Request] --> B{In Cache?}
    B -- Yes --> C[Apply Cached Result]
    B -- No --> D[Call Entitlement Module]
    D --> E{Allowed?}
    E -- Yes --> F[Cache & Execute]
    E -- No --> G[Reject Request]
    F --> H[Apply Content Filters/Select Lists]

title: Content-Based Security 🔍
content: Restrict visibility at the **record level** using filter predicates.
Example: A user can only see orders where `/Region == 'EMEA'`.
• Enforced by the server on every message.
• Completely transparent to the application.
• Allows multi-tenant topics where users only see 'their' data. 🏘️

title: Field-Level Security 🙈
content: Hide sensitive data using **Select Lists**.
Example: Strip the `/CreditCardNumber` field from messages for regular users, but keep it for the Billing service.
• `-/CC_Number` -> Removes the field.
• `+/ID, +/Price` -> Only includes specified fields.
Privacy by design! 🕵️

title: Enterprise Integration Modules 🏢
content: AMPS doesn't just do 'simple' auth; it scales to the enterprise:
• **Multimethod**: Integrates with LDAP and Kerberos. 🛡️
• **OAuth**: Modern web-scale authentication. 🌐
• **RESTful (HTTP)**: Ask an external web service for permissions. 🌍
• **Simple Access**: Regex-based allow/deny lists for easy setup.

title: Protecting Data in Transit: TLS/SSL 🚄
content: Encryption is vital for security over untrusted networks.
• Standard TLS/SSL for client-server links.
• **Mutual TLS (mTLS)**: Server verifies the client's certificate too! 🤝
• Independent of the Auth/Entitlement system – defense in depth.

title: Outbound Security & Authenticators 📤
content: AMPS itself needs to 'log on' to other systems (like for replication).
**Authenticators** handle this:
• Provide credentials to downstream instances.
• Can run external commands to fetch tokens.
• Supports Kerberos and LDAP for outbound links.

title: Best Practices for AMPS Security 🏆
content: • **Use Explicit Logon**: Always know who is connecting.
• **Enable TLS**: Never send sensitive data in the clear.
• **Least Privilege**: Only grant the permissions needed for the job.
• **Regularly Reset Caches**: Ensure permission changes take effect.
• **Monitor Admin Access**: The admin console is powerful – protect it! ⚡

title: Summary & Key Takeaways 📝
content: • Security is baked into the core of AMPS, not an afterthought.
• Plugins allow integration with ANY enterprise system.
• Content and Field-level security provide fine-grained control.
• A secure AMPS instance is a happy (and compliant) instance! 😊
